name: simulate-roth-conversion-boundary
why: Measured reach for the pure aggregate Roth-conversion planner, its protected live-reservation replay and the caller band that invokes both, publishes the planner snapshot and consumes the allocation. Block T's four hostile members run in all four equivalence modes: T1 combines deferred-RMD Map owner order, a reverse Plan-order multi-account reserve, duplicate Roth ids with distinct opening balances, two-owner exact-cent allocation and ordered source/destination publication; T2 makes the required subtract/add restoration move a binary64 leaf and exercises counterfactual rollback/re-entry; T3 reaches household refusal; T4 reaches an allocated result with no convertible owner, slices or draws. Focused tests separately pin live object identity, cross-owner operation order, restoration after a deliberately thrown reserved-scope callback, and rejection of an injected destination identity absent from the allocator inventory: a JSON dump cannot observe those identity/order invariants when final economic values agree, and no validated Plan can make the production allocator return that hostile identity graph.

entries.note: T1 reaches both owners, skips nontraditional and other-owner rows, exhausts p1's one-dollar tail, skips its zero-dollar IRA and continues into the earlier source. T2 supplies the cancellation-sensitive reservation. Inherited-account exclusion is pinned by the focused helper suite. The remaining cold nullish owner fallback is a supported structural contract but cannot be selected by corpus data because Plan validation requires every traditional account to name an individual owner.

readingTheCounts: A member count proves that at least one line in the named range executed. The reach command additionally fails on any cold executable whole line inside a reached range. JavaScript line coverage cannot distinguish every operand or branch sharing a physical line, so the report's cold sub-line regions and these notes must be read together with the focused helper and hostile delegation tests.
